metadata.name: sra_cctp_adapter
metadata.description: SRA CCTP Adapter — Circle CCTP v2 source deposit + destination mint verification

accounts.name: fee_payer
docs: Pays the tx fee and the CCTP `MessageSent` event-account rent.

accounts.name: adapter_authority
docs: the same address via `seeds::program = adapter_program.key()`. Owns
`adapter_custody` and signs the burn directly (no delegate approval).

accounts.name: input_mint
docs: The burn decreases the supply, so the mint is writable.

accounts.name: remote_token_messenger
docs: must equal `destination_domain`).

accounts.name: message_sent_event_data
docs: Ephemeral keypair account CCTP initializes with the `MessageSent`
payload; co-signs the transaction, rent paid by `fee_payer`.

accounts.name: fee_payer
docs: Pays the tx fee (gas-sponsorship parity with the deposit flow).

accounts.name: owner
docs: SRA owner = authority; must sign and match `sra_config.owner`.

accounts.name: adapter_authority
docs: out of `adapter_custody`. Address constrained via seeds + bump.

accounts.name: message_transmitter
docs: raw bytes (never CPI'd), so its layout is validated by
`deserialize_message_transmitter` in the handler body.

accounts.name: used_nonce
docs: seeds + owner; proves the mint executed. Parsed exact-layout in-body.

accounts.name: route
docs: The committed destination route the mint is being verified against. An
`Account` here requires it to be a genuine handler-owned route.

errors.name: PreparedNonceUnavailable
errors.msg: Mint nonce does not contain a prepared deposit

errors.name: NothingToRecover
errors.msg: No tokens in adapter custody to recover

errors.name: UnsupportedChain
errors.msg: Target chain has no CCTP domain mapping

errors.name: InvalidFinalityThreshold
errors.msg: CCTP finality threshold must be 1000 or 2000

errors.name: QuoteExceedsNetAfterFee
errors.msg: Committed output exceeds the net input after the CCTP max fee

errors.name: MalformedMessage
errors.msg: CCTP message bytes do not parse as a supported burn message

errors.name: InvalidAttestation
errors.msg: Attestation does not verify against the enabled attesters

errors.name: InvalidTransmitterState
errors.msg: MessageTransmitter state account is malformed or inconsistent

errors.name: NonceNotUsed
errors.msg: Used-nonce receipt does not prove an executed mint

errors.name: NonceMismatch
errors.msg: Message nonce does not match the supplied nonce

errors.name: InvalidRecipientProgram
errors.msg: Message recipient is not the CCTP TokenMessengerMinter program

errors.name: DestinationDomainMismatch
errors.msg: Message destination domain is not this chain's CCTP domain

errors.name: MintRecipientMismatch
errors.msg: Mint recipient is not the route vault for the expected mint

errors.name: SourceDomainMismatch
errors.msg: Message source domain does not map to the route's source chain

errors.name: FeeExceedsMaxFee
errors.msg: Executed fee exceeds max fee, or max fee is not below the amount

errors.name: FreshRouteRequired
errors.msg: Initial enrollment must immediately follow creation of the handler route

types.name: AccountTemplate
docs: Ordered account-slot policy for a `VerifiedCpi`'s inner instruction. Slot
order matches the inner CPI's account list; each slot is pinned by the
handler (`Fixed`) or supplied by the relayer as routing (`Free`).

types.name: AddressBookEntry
docs: Per-address-book-root owner-managed (source_mint, chain, target_token) -> decimals registry.
`target_decimals = 0` is a tombstone/disabled entry, mirroring zeroed EVM TokenInfo.
PDA seeds: ["address_book", address_book_root, source_mint, chain_id.to_le_bytes(), target_token]

fields.name: target_decimals
docs: Decimals of `target_token` on the target chain. Serves three roles:
(a) canonical record for downstream amount math, (b) EVM-parity
existence sentinel, (c) tombstone marker when `0`. Tokens with 0
real decimals are not representable here — not a concern for USDC
and other bridgeable tokens, but worth knowing.

types.name: AddressBookRoot
docs: Owner-managed source address-book namespace. The root account is initialized
explicitly and then committed inside immutable `SourceHandlerData`.

fields.name: message_sent_event_data
docs: Ephemeral account holding the CCTP `MessageSent` payload; the off-chain
key for this deposit (Iris assigns the nonce after the fact).

fields.name: input_amount
docs: Net of protocol fee (`PrepareParams::net_input_amount`).

fields.name: max_fee
docs: CCTP fee cap; the destination-side `fee_executed` is bounded by this.

fields.name: min_finality_threshold
docs: CCTP v2 finality; canonical values are `FINALITY_THRESHOLD_FAST`
(1000) and `FINALITY_THRESHOLD_FINALIZED` (2000), and the adapter

fields.name: fill_id
docs: The Iris-assigned message nonce — the destination-side fill identity.

types.name: FixedRole
docs: Handler-controlled roles a `Fixed` slot can take. `Source`, `Destination`,
`SigningAuthority`, and `OutputMint` MUST appear in every template (enforced by
`validate_action_config`) so a relayer cannot redirect the input or output, and
so the handler reads the output mint from a pinned account.

types.name: MinOut
docs: Minimum-output reference for a `VerifiedCpi`'s post-fee balance-diff gate.

types.name: MintNonce
docs: Persistent nonce per `(sra_config, source_mint)`. The owner-signed deposit
flow will create it lazily and increment it per source-mint deposit.
PDA seeds: ["mint_nonce", sra_config, source_mint]

types.name: SolanaAction
docs: A pre-registered action to execute on the destination chain after fill
finalization. v1: `SplTransfer` (static, exact-match accounts) and
`VerifiedCpi` (dynamic accounts, outcome-verified).

fields.name: amount_bps
docs: Basis points of the execution vault balance to transfer (e.g., 10000 = 100%).

fields.name: program_id
docs: Pinned program — checked loader-owned-executable + exact pubkey at execution.

fields.name: input_mint
docs: Token spent from the vault (usually `expected_mint`).

fields.name: input_bps
docs: Basis points of the vault moved into the scratch source — the input bound.

fields.name: output_mint
docs: Fungible receipt the engine balance-diffs (swap output, vault share, LST, …).

fields.name: allow_permissioned_output
docs: Opt-in for Token-2022 permissioned (perm-delegate / frozen) output mints.

types.name: SolanaSraRoute
docs: Deterministic destination address for EVM->Solana fills.
PDA seeds: ["sra_route", owner, config_hash, salt]
config_hash = keccak256(borsh(owner, source_chain_id, expected_mint, action_config))

fields.name: action_config
docs: The committed action list, stored typed so later instructions read it
directly instead of re-verifying a relayer-supplied copy. Also folded into
the route's config_hash (the PDA seed), so the address inherently commits
to it.

fields.name: allowed_executors
docs: Owner-managed; not in `route_config_hash` (mutable, like `allowed_adapters`).
Empty = no caller can `execute_actions`.

types.name: SourceHandlerData
docs: Owner-installed source policy. Committed at SRA install via
`handler_data_hash` (folded into the SRA's PDA identity) and re-supplied,
then re-authenticated, on every deposit. The routing tuple
(`target_chain_id` / `recipient` / `target_token`) is part of the immutable
identity, mirroring the
EVM `RouteConfig` that `trigger()` reads from storage and a caller cannot
redirect (see `sra-stx/src/handler/SRAHandler.sol`). Every deposit must echo
this exact routing in `PrepareParams`; `validate_and_prepare` rejects any
divergence. Changing the route means a new SRA at a new address — the Solana
analogue of the EVM clone-proxy + `_onInstall` model.

types.name: SraConfig
docs: One source-side SRA per `(owner, final_handler, handler_data_hash, salt)`.
PDA seeds: ["sra", owner, config_hash, salt]
config_hash = keccak256(owner ‖ final_handler ‖ handler_data_hash)

types.name: VerifiedFill
docs: Adapter-owned verification artifact. Created by this adapter once it has
confirmed a CCTP mint, then read by the handler across the program boundary
to authorize `finalize_fill`. A vault-balance increase alone cannot prove a
legitimate bridge fill — this account is the trust boundary that does.
The struct name must stay `VerifiedFill`: the handler hardcodes
`sha256("account:VerifiedFill")[..8]` as the discriminator it accepts from
every adapter.
The post-discriminator field layout is a cross-program ABI contract with
`sra_common::types::VerifiedFillData`. The handler reads this account as raw bytes
(it must accept fills from multiple adapter programs, each with its own
program id, so it cannot import this type) and deserializes via that plain
struct, requiring an exact layout match. Any field reorder, addition, or
removal here is a breaking change and MUST be mirrored there — the round-trip
and discriminator tests below fail loudly if the two drift.
